motivation: Q84's 13 aggregate flow coordinates and K-neighbor sensitivity did not demonstrate gain. Test whether preserving each of the 40 number identities and their cross-sectional state yields a more informative field than aggregating the draw into a small global vector.
quantitative_hypothesis: A 40-node x 6-feature field, with a separate 40x40 pair co-occurrence residual graph, may condition the existing Q84 equal-weight Borda ranking more effectively than aggregate flow analogues. One of 12 fixed field operators is selected on Discovery only. The primary practical target is at least +0.10 Top20 hits/target over equal42 on Blind OOS, with paired block-bootstrap lower bound >0 and global Holm-adjusted exact-null p<0.05.

node_features: cross-sectional z frequency rate over last 5 draws
cross-sectional z frequency rate over last 20 draws
cross-sectional z frequency rate over last 80 draws
cross-sectional z log(1 + draws since last occurrence)
field.pair_graph: Symmetric 40x40 log ratio of pair co-occurrence rates in recent 80 versus preceding up to 320 draws; 20 pseudo-draws at uniform pair probability; diagonal zero; graph signal is adjacency multiplied by tanh(FLOW node signal).
field.normalization: Each feature is standardized cross-sectionally over the 40 numbers at each target; all inputs use draws strictly before target.

candidates.score: z(41 - equal-weight Q84 Borda rank) + alpha*z(field_variant)
candidates.selection: Discovery only: highest mean Top20 hits/target; tie lower mean actual-number rank, then stable strategy ID.

walkforward.split_rule: First floor(60%) Discovery, next through floor(80%) Validation, remainder Blind OOS.
walkforward.cutoff_rule: For target archive index i, all node and pair-graph features use draws[0:i] only. Rank all 40 numbers before reading/scoring target i. Flow analogue memory admits the current target only after scoring it.
walkforward.target_ledger: One row per target with previous-day cutoff, actual quintet, split, field-state SHA256 and complete 40-number rank permutations for all 14 models.

inference.null: Per-target Hypergeometric(40,k,5) hit count under independent uniform 5-of-40 reference; discrete upper-tail convolution across each fixed split.
inference.multiple_testing: One global Holm-Bonferroni family across 14 models x 3 splits x 3 endpoints = 126 tests.
inference.paired_comparison: Circular moving-block bootstrap, block length 20, 2,000 replicates, fixed seeds, selected Discovery field candidate vs equal42 and flow K50 on Validation and Blind OOS.
primary_gate: Selected field candidate Blind OOS Top20 mean >= 2.5
Blind OOS paired Top20 lift vs equal42 >= +0.10 hits/target
selected field candidate global Holm-adjusted Blind OOS Top20 p < 0.05

guardrails: No target or future row enters any feature, threshold, graph edge or ranking before that target is scored.
Only Discovery chooses the field variant and alpha; Validation and Blind OOS do not tune parameters.
All 14 models and all endpoints/splits are included in one global Holm family.
Historical Blind OOS is already exposed to prior SONAR research; it is exploratory, not a virgin holdout.
No automatic merge, engine promotion, prospective shadow insertion or immutable freeze modification.
The pair graph is a historical association descriptor, not a claim of physical coupling.
limitations: Finite 12-operator field grammar; it does not exhaust all possible functions of the 40x6 field.
The uniform independent-draw null is a reference calibration, not proof of the generating mechanism.
Historical split results cannot replace prospective confirmation.
next_action: Execute walk-forward, replay all 14x40 rank vectors and exact null p-values, persist append-only outputs, then request human review and a prospective freeze.
